passage:
A student found a translated diary written by a nurse during a major war. The diary did not describe famous battles. It described cold rooms, tired hands, missing family, and small acts of kindness.
The student had always imagined history as large events. The diary showed history from inside one person's day.
In class, he said the diary made the war feel less like a chapter title and more like human life under pressure.
The teacher said personal records are valuable because they show what official reports often miss.
A diary may not explain everything, but it can make the past harder to ignore.
